text: Then suddenly, as he rested there. <break time="0.8s" /> The room was filled with the strong, sweet odor of mignonette. <break time="0.8s" /> A scent so clear. <break time="0.8s" /> That it seemed almost like a living visitor. <break time="0.8s" /> What, dear, he cried aloud. <break time="0.8s" /> As if someone had called to him. <break time="0.8s" /> And he sprang up and turned around. <break time="0.8s" /> To see who was there. <break time="0.8s" /> It was the scent. <break time="0.8s" /> That she had loved and made her own. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was certain. <break time="0.8s" /> That she had been in this very room. <break time="0.8s" /> Not long before. <break time="0.8s" /> In the dresser and drawers he found hairpins. <break time="0.8s" /> A worn handkerchief smelling of heliotrope. <break time="0.8s" /> Buttons, and a theater program. <break time="0.8s" /> But none of them could tell him about her. <break time="0.8s" /> He held a black satin hair bow. <break time="0.8s" /> For a long moment. <break time="0.8s" /> But it too was a common thing. <break time="0.8s" /> An ordinary ornament. <break time="0.8s" /> That told no tales about its owner. <break time="0.8s" /> He crawled over the floor. <break time="0.8s" /> And searched every corner. <break time="0.8s" /> Calling Yes, dear, to the empty air. <break time="0.8s" /> But he found nothing. <break time="0.8s" /> Except old corks and cigarettes. <break time="0.8s" /> He hurried down to the housekeeper. <break time="0.8s" /> And begged her to tell him. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had lived in the room. <break time="0.8s" /> Before he came. <break time="0.8s" /> Miss Sprowls and Missus Mooney. <break time="0.8s" /> Left a week ago Tuesday, she answered. <break time="0.8s" /> Describing a short, stout woman with black hair. <break time="0.8s" /> And then she named other tenants. <break time="0.8s" /> From long before.
